title: F1 in Mexico City: Yet another Ferrari fiasco, but that’s not all
gist: At the Mexico City GP, Kimi Antonelli became F1's youngest-ever champion while Max Verstappen won for Red Bull after Ferrari's Leclerc and Hamilton raced each other and threw away a likely 1-2. Also: Cadillac miscounted Colton Herta's super license points, Haas benched Esteban Ocon, and reliability failures hit Aston Martin and Cadillac.

insights.claim: Kimi Antonelli sealed the Formula 1 World Drivers' Championship in Mexico City a few months after turning 20, becoming the sport's youngest-ever champion.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Mercedes has a generational young star as champion.

insights.claim: Verstappen won the race, with the Red Bull power unit showing superior power output over Ferrari's even at altitude.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Red Bull's power unit holds an edge in thin-air conditions.

insights.claim: Ferrari threw away a likely 1-2 when Leclerc and Hamilton raced each other; Leclerc gained an advantage off-track at turn 4 and his five-second penalty was too small to matter, letting Verstappen take the lead.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Lack of team orders is costing Ferrari wins.

insights.claim: The author attributes the loss to Leclerc's unwillingness to support his teammate, which he says explains why Leclerc has 27 pole positions but only nine wins in eight years.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Driver temperament is a measurable drag on conversion of poles to wins.
insights.quote: showed us why he has 27 pole positions but only nine wins in eight years
insights.locator: Both Ferraris got off the line well

insights.claim: Hamilton took his first Ferrari pole and 105th career pole in Mexico City.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Ferrari's qualifying pace is real even if race execution fails.
insights.locator: For most of this year, Ferrari

insights.claim: Hamilton warned that losses would continue unless action is taken and a deep, serious conversation is had about teammates working together.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Internal Ferrari conflict likely to escalate.
insights.quote: And that will continue unless action is taken, and a real deep, serious conversation is had

insights.claim: Unlike Mercedes, which made drivers pay for damage after collisions, and McLaren's Papaya rules, Ferrari lets both drivers race freely, and if it keeps giving away wins Fred Vasseur's position becomes increasingly untenable.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.quote: if Ferrari keeps giving away race wins like this, his position has to be increasingly untenable
insights.locator: Other teams have laid down clear rules

insights.claim: Cadillac miscounted Colton Herta's super license points by relying on IndyCar's erroneous website; he had 35 rather than 36 points and still needs one more of the required 40.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Administrative sloppiness delays Cadillac's plan to replace Bottas with Herta.
insights.locator: But it turns out they hadn’t added

insights.claim: Cadillac nearly lost its chance to enter F1 in 2024 when FIA emails went to its spam folder.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Pattern of paperwork failures at the new team.

insights.claim: Bottas' Cadillac suffered a front-left suspension failure on lap 44 causing a heavy crash and red flag, on top of season-long front-brake overheating problems.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin

insights.claim: Haas benched Esteban Ocon after a dispute over tire choice, replacing him with reserve Ryo Hirakawa; Ocon will not return in 2027, with Rafael Camara taking the seat.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Likely end of Ocon's F1 career for now.
